title: Vande Mataram Rendered at Red Fort for First Time as India Marks 80th Independence Day
excerpt: PM Modi leads celebrations featuring the national song at the Red Fort, as Parliament passes landmark bill giving Vande Mataram legal protection equal to the National Anthem.
body:
• Vande Mataram was rendered at New Delhi's Red Fort during Independence Day celebrations for the first time in India's history.
  • Parliament passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, giving the national song the same legal protection as the National Anthem.
  • The government endorsed the full six-stanza version of Vande Mataram for official events, with standing mandatory during its rendition.
  • Independence Day invitation cards featured Fundamental Duties and the complete Vande Mataram lyrics, replacing the traditional Red Fort image with the new PM's office building.

India's national song Vande Mataram was rendered at the Red Fort during Independence Day celebrations on August 15 for the first time, marking a watershed moment in the country's 80th year of independence. Prime Minister Narendra Modi led the celebrations at the historic Delhi landmark, where the song composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay in 1882 was performed as part of the official ceremony.

The rendition comes as part of the government's broader campaign to elevate the national song's status in India's public life, coinciding with the 150th anniversary of the composition's creation.

Legislative Milestone

The performance followed Parliament's passage of the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, during the ongoing Monsoon Session. The legislation extends to Vande Mataram the same statutory protection that the National Anthem, Jana Gana Mana, has enjoyed under the 1971 Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act.

https://x.com/MIB_India/status/2088467084238008601

Under the amended law, obstructing or insulting the rendition of Vande Mataram will attract a prison term of up to three years, a fine, or both. The Rajya Sabha passed the bill amid protests and a walkout by the Opposition, according to reports.

New Guidelines for the National Song

In May 2026, the Union government endorsed the full six-stanza version of Vande Mataram as the official rendition for government events, fixing the standard duration at three minutes and ten seconds. The Home Ministry directive requires all attendees to stand at attention during the song's performance.

When both Vande Mataram and the National Anthem are performed at the same event, the national song must be rendered first. The guidelines prescribe mandatory rendition at Republic Day and Independence Day ceremonies, government functions, school and college assemblies, and events involving the President, Vice President, or Governors.

Symbolic Shifts in the Celebrations

The Defence Ministry's Independence Day invitation cards this year carried the full text of Fundamental Duties under Article 51A of the Constitution alongside the complete lyrics of Vande Mataram in both Hindi and English, according to The Hindu BusinessLine. The card's design replaced the traditional Red Fort image with the newly constructed Prime Minister's office, called 'Sewa Teerth,' inscribed with the Sanskrit phrase 'Nagarika devo bhava.'

Approximately 5,000 special guests attended the celebrations at the Red Fort, with over 1,500 people from various states and union territories dressed in traditional attire. The Indian Air Force served as the coordinating service for this year's Independence Day ceremony.

Historical Context

Vande Mataram, first published in Chattopadhyay's 1882 novel Anand Math, served as a rallying cry during India's independence movement. The Constituent Assembly had originally accorded national song status only to the opening portions, while adopting Jana Gana Mana as the National Anthem — a distinction rooted in the later stanzas' invocation of Hindu goddesses.

The government's push to elevate the song reflects the BJP's long-standing emphasis on cultural nationalism. The Republic Day parade earlier in January 2026 featured a Ministry of Culture tableau celebrating '150 Years of Vande Mataram,' with a representation of the original manuscript accompanied by folk artists from across the country.

What's Next

With the legal framework now in place, Vande Mataram is expected to become a fixture at official government events across the country. State governments and educational institutions have been directed to implement the new guidelines, though the mandatory standing rule does not apply in informal settings such as cinema halls or documentary screenings.

The Ministry of Home Affairs also announced 1,090 police, fire, and civil defence medals on the occasion of Independence Day, comprising 233 gallantry medals, 99 President's Medals for Distinguished Service, and 758 medals for meritorious service.
